asof: Settles Tue 17 Nov 2026 · written Wed 18 Nov
headline: Risk-off bid lands on the peak: U7 6bp lower at 4.71% and the Z6/M7 target is hit; the strip still prices just over three hikes.
summary: SR3 bull-flattened around the peak as the tech selloff deepened: M7 fell 5.5bp in rate to 4.675%, U7 6bp to 4.71% and Z7 5.5bp to 4.685%, while Z6 slipped only 0.75bp to 4.29% and H7 3bp to 4.55%, and Z8 through Z9 fell 3bp. Over this week's two sessions U7 is down 11bp, Z7 11.5bp and M7 9.5bp against 1.5bp in Z6, but from the 30 October settle H7 through H8 are still 19–19.5bp higher and Z6 14.5bp. U7 remains the peak at 4.71%, 78bp over the 3.93% SOFR fixing and down from 4.82% on Friday, with 16bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is a little over three hikes, in line with Bank of America's and Deutsche Bank's three-hike calls, above Goldman's two and below Musalem's case for up to four by spring.
drivers: Flight to quality from the tech rout

Equities fell again ahead of Nvidia's results and network outages briefly spooked markets, and two-year yields fell 4.2bp to 4.789% on Tuesday after 3.1bp on Monday. The bid was strongest in the mid-2027 contracts: U7 fell 6bp and M7 5.5bp, against 0.75bp in Z6.
Musalem pushes, Williams and the data rule out 50bp

Musalem said several hikes are likely needed before spring 2027, implying a move at each meeting through April, while Williams said the situation does not call for dramatic action. Fed funds futures now price 25.4bp for 9 December with only a 1.4% chance of 50bp, and FedWatch slipped to 26.0bp for December and 61.3bp by March from 27.1bp and 62.3bp.

October retail sales rose 0.2% as expected, but sales ex-autos rose 0.6% against 0.4% forecast and the control group beat too, with GDPNow at 3.4%. Import prices jumped 1.1% against 0.7% expected, with ex-fuel and food up 0.9%, so Z6 barely moved and Z6/H7 narrowed 2.25bp to +26bp.
Funding firmer after refunding settlement; oil steadier

SOFR fixed at 3.93% on 16 November, up from 3.90% and 5bp over EFFR at 3.88%, with reverse repo usage at just $0.351bn; U6 edged up 0.25bp to 3.93%. Brent settled $0.70 higher at $93.14, still down about 20% this month, which helped the 2028–29 contracts rally 3bp.
spreads: The belly led and the curve flattened from Z6 to the peak. U6/Z6 fell 1bp to +36bp (+13.75bp on the month), Z6/H7 2.25bp to +26bp (−3.5bp week-to-date, +5bp on the month), H7/M7 2.5bp to +12.5bp (−4.5bp on the week, unchanged on the month) and M7/U7 0.5bp to +3.5bp; U7/Z7 rose 0.5bp to −2.5bp, so U7 stays the peak by 2.5bp over Z7 and 3.5bp over M7. Z6/Z7 fell 4.75bp to +39.5bp (−10bp on the week, +4.5bp on the month) and Z6/M7 4.75bp to +38.5bp (−8bp on the week, +5bp on the month). Past the peak the inversion narrowed as the back lagged: Z7/H8 rose 1.5bp to −3bp, Z7/Z8 2.5bp to −10.5bp (−3bp on the month) and U7/Z8 3bp to −13bp (+1bp on the week, −3bp on the month), while Z8/Z9 held at −3bp and the 2029 spreads sit between −1.5bp and 0. The H7/M7/U7 fly fell 2bp to +9bp (−3bp on the week, +0.5bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 1bp to +6bp (−0.5bp on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Monday's, prices 25.4bp for 9 December (98.6% for 25bp, 1.4% for 50bp), 43.5bp by January, 61.2bp by March, 77.8bp by June and an 83.5bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.715%). That compares with 27.5bp, 46bp, 63.7bp, 82.5bp and a 90.5bp peak on Friday, 20.4bp, 26.5bp, 37.6bp, 48.4bp and 50.5bp a week earlier on 9 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 7.8bp on the month and the peak 26.5bp, but both have come off since Thursday. Tuesday's FedWatch reading of 26.0bp for December and 61.3bp by March shows little change at the front. Adding a 2bp SOFR premium, Monday's ZQ path implies about 4.25% for Z6's December–March window and 4.725% for U7, so Z6 at 4.29% sits 4bp above it and U7 at 4.71% about 1.5bp below after Tuesday's rally; the 16 November fixing ran 5bp over EFFR, which would lift those fair values by 3bp. Bank of America and Deutsche Bank expect three hikes and Goldman two, while Musalem argued for up to four by spring; the strip now sits near the three-hike consensus, not above it.

ideas.title: Z6/M7 target hit: bank it and re-sell on a bounce
ideas.trade: Sell SR3Z6, buy SR3M7 (sell the Z6/M7 spread) at +42bp
ideas.why: The short from +47bp hit its +39bp target as the spread fell 4.75bp to +38.5bp, 8.5bp in our favour, so we take profit. The view stands: Z6 to M7 still prices about one and a half hikes after the first quarter of 2027, but after an 8bp fall this week we would rather sell a hawkish bounce from the minutes or PCE. That is 7bp to target against 4.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A fresh risk-off leg could push M7 lower faster than Z6 and leave the spread below +42bp, so the re-entry never fills.

ideas.title: Buy Z6/H7 into the minutes and PCE
ideas.trade: Buy SR3Z6, sell SR3H7 (buy the Z6/H7 spread)
ideas.why: The U7/Z8 flattener is closed: the back lagged Tuesday's rally and the spread rose 3bp to −13bp, through the −14bp stop that Friday's revised settle had already touched, a 4.5bp loss from entry. Z6/H7 fell 2.25bp to +26bp even after firm retail sales and import prices, and Musalem's hike-a-meeting path to April is not in H7 at 4.55%. It pays if hawkish minutes or PCE add hikes in early 2027, the risk to our core; 6bp to target against 4bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: A deeper equity selloff or a soft PCE print could take January–March hikes out and push the spread below +22bp.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract into bill settlement and month-end

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: The funding risk we flagged showed up: SOFR fixed at 3.93% on 16 November, 5bp over EFFR, and U6 rose 0.25bp to 3.93% while the rest of the strip rallied 0.75–6bp. Only U6's last week sees the 9 December decision, now priced 98.6% for 25bp, and $300bn of bills settle on 24 November ahead of month-end, with reverse repo usage near zero.
ideas.risk: If month-end passes quietly and SOFR slips back to 3.90%, U6 would gain a couple of bp.
